newsitem.title: UK: EDF Man raises estimate for EU 96/97 sugar output.
newsitem.headline: EDF Man raises estimate for EU 96/97 sugar output.

text.p: Trade house E D & F Man on Tuesday raised its forecast for sugar production in the European Union (EU) by 200,000 tonnes to 15.83 million tonnes white value for 1996/97 as sugar contents rise in key producing nations.
The revised estimate would be 210,000 tonnes higher than in 1995/96 but still some one million tonnes down on the average output achieved in the 1992/93 and 1993/94 seasons, Man said.
In its latest monthly report, Man said sugar contents in France and Germany -- the EU's two largest producers -- were reported to be high and so national forecasts had been raised.

France should now produce 4.1 million tonnes of sugar and the yield per hectare would be close to the 9.8 tonnes per hectare achieved last season when a final crop of 4.2 million tonnes was produced on a larger area.
Last month Man forecast French production at 4.05 million tonnes.
Man also raised its estimate for Germany's 1996/97 sugar production to 4.06 million tonnes from 4.05 in October. German output reached 3.83 million tonnes in 1995/96, it said.
